name: Argon
occurrence: Third most abundant gas in the atmosphere (~0.93%), far more common in air than CO₂.
majorUses: Filling incandescent and fluorescent light bulbs
Preserving documents and wine bottles from oxidation
notableCharacteristics: Its name comes from the Greek 'argos', meaning 'lazy' or 'inactive', a nod to its near-total chemical unreactivity.
ncertRelevance: abundance in atmosphere versus other noble gases
whyHere: A full 3s² 3p⁶ octet leaves it with no drive to bond, and its relative abundance in air (versus rarer helium/neon) comes from being a stable end-product of potassium-40 radioactive decay in Earth's crust.
didYouKnow: Argon makes up roughly 1% of every breath you take, yet it does absolutely nothing once inhaled or exhaled.
genZNote: Named 'the lazy one' by ancient Greek logic. Fills lightbulbs and welding tanks without lifting an electron.
